structured_output.world_model:
W3 (cost lens), after E008. Labels: the branch tip has HYP epochs = 9.5 at batch 2000, which is 25 steps per epoch and about 238 steps. E007 ran at 10 epochs, and E008 was really a 10 → 9.5 cut. Ideas that say "at 9 epochs" mean the tip at 9.5.

What was measured:
- E004: compile plus fused SGD cut 14%. E003: a recompile leak inside timed code cost +3 s. Leaks are the dominant risk for any new shape or graph.
- E005: Lookahead/EMA gave +0.97 pp for about 0.06 s.
- E006: Muon gave +0.66 pp for +4% time.
- E007: resizing 24/28/32 at 40/30/30% cut 22% of time and 0.59 pp of accuracy.
- E008: cutting 0.5 epoch saved 0.35 s (−4.8%) and cost only 0.18 pp. With Muon plus EMA the epoch slope is flatter, about 0.35 pp per epoch, not the 0.6-0.7 pp per epoch seen without them.

Budget model: time ≈ F + V × (pixel-weighted epoch fraction).
- F ≈ 0.8 s (H2D, eigh, pad, augment).
- At the tip, V ≈ 8.2 s full-res-equivalent for 9.5 epochs, with a pixel fraction of 0.755.
- Rates per unit of accuracy:
  - Epochs: about 0.35 s per 0.18 pp, so about 2 s per pp.
  - Resizing: about 3.5 s per pp (E007).
  - Both now cost similar seconds per pp at the margin. Resizing gets worse as more of the run moves to ≤20 px and as the 32-px tail shrinks.
- Margin: 0.7572 − 0.753 = 0.42 pp. Against a 40-seed safety bar near 0.756 the margin is only about 0.1-0.15 pp. Further time cuts must therefore be paired with accuracy-adding, near-free changes (LR-to-0, LS or wd tuning), or come from pure systems savings.

Systems: at about 25 ms per step at batch 2000 the GPU is mostly saturated. Launch overhead with compiled forward/backward plus compiled Muon is likely ≤3%, so CUDA graphs gain little and carry leak risk. FLOPs breakdown (32 px): group2 dominates; group3 is about 37%. Going 576 → 512 cuts total FLOPs by about 5.5%, which is about 4% of wall time.

Noise: per seed, compiled runs are deterministic. Per-seed std is about 0.2-0.35 pp, so the 3-seed SE is about 0.15-0.2 pp. Time noise is 1-2%.

My misses: I was low on the accuracy of EMA, Muon and resizing (prior shifted up). On E008 my time forecast was too optimistic (6.55 forecast vs 6.98 measured). The fixed cost F is larger, or the per-step cost less pixel-proportional, than I assumed, so I shrink predicted savings from resolution and width by about 25%.

Unsure about:
- whether ≤20 px degrades accuracy super-linearly;
- the 40-seed offset versus seeds 0-2;
- whether LR-to-0 adds anything on top of EMA;
- how much cuDNN autotune for new shapes in BN recalibration costs inside timed train.

forecasts.reason: Free in time. The gain is probably 0-0.25 pp because EMA already does most of the end-averaging, and a delta under 0.3 pp is within 3-seed noise.
The pixel fraction drops from 0.755 to 0.64, saving about 0.7 s. But 20 px and a 32-px tail cut from 30% to 20% likely cost about 0.5-0.7 pp, which probably breaks the 0.753 bar.
About 5.5% fewer FLOPs gives about a 3.5% wall-time cut, borderline against the 4% threshold. Accuracy loss is about 0.2 pp, which leaves a thin margin.
The recipe is unchanged, so the measured metrics replicate E008 deterministically. H4.1.2 is about the E005 recipe and only offline data speaks to it.
At batch 2000 steps are GPU-bound (about 25 ms each), so launch savings are ≤3%. Float LR and Lookahead steps add capture and leak risk.

Lookahead already averages the BN buffers, so the gain is about 0.1 pp. The new 5k batch shape on the eager train path costs cuDNN autotune plus a forward pass of more than 0.15 s, or it triggers error_on_recompile through the compiled path.

cruxes: Is the 40-seed mean of the tip recipe at or above about 0.755, or does it sit below seeds 0-2? This decides whether any of the 0.42 pp margin can still be spent on time.
Does dropping to 20 px and shrinking the 32-px tail cost accuracy super-linearly, beyond about 0.5 pp? This decides whether resizing or epochs is the cheaper next dial.
Can a near-free accuracy gain (LR-to-0, LS or wd retune) of 0.2-0.3 pp be found to fund a further 0.5-epoch or width cut?
